mainTopic: Foods withheld from the כהן גדול, side-discussions on גרגיר and on the traveling marriages of רב and רב נחמן, and a new משנה on the כהן גדול's oath and his night of learning before יום הכפורים
overview: This עמוד opens with the end of a ברייתא listing foods not given to the כהן גדול before יום כיפור, because they may cause קרי. The mention of גרגיר (arugula) leads to a short side-discussion: it is the אורות of the פסוק, and it is good for the eyes. The mention of eggs leads to רב's advice that a guest should not eat eggs or sleep in his host's garment. The גמרא then tells how רב and רב נחמן, when traveling, would announce that they wished to marry a local woman for their stay. It challenges this from רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, who warns that children of such marriages may unknowingly marry each other; the answer is that the children of famous רבנן are well known. A second challenge from רבא, that a woman who agrees to marry must count שבעה נקיים, gets two answers: messengers were sent ahead, or there was only seclusion and no real relationship. Then a new משנה describes how the זקני כהונה take the כהן גדול to בית אבטינס and make him swear not to change the עבודה, after which everyone cries. The משנה ends by describing how he is kept awake all night with Torah learning and readings from איוב, עזרא, דברי הימים and דניאל.

steps.title: End of the list of foods that may cause קרי
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes listing foods not given to the כהן גדול before יום כיפור: cress, purslane, eggs and arugula.
steps.simpleTranslation: And cress, and purslane, and eggs, and arugula.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the end of a list that began on the previous עמוד. It names foods the כהן גדול is not fed on ערב יום כיפור because they might cause טומאת קרי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern is that the כהן גדול must stay טהור to do the עבודה on יום כיפור. Each food on the list was thought to heat the body or increase desire. Two items here, eggs and גרגיר, become the starting points for the side-discussions that follow.
steps.confusionAlert: This line has no opening words because it is the tail end of a ברייתא that started on the previous part of the דף. It is not a new statement.

phrases.english: And cress and purslane
phrases.notes: Continuing the list of foods withheld from the כהן גדול

phrases.english: and eggs and arugula.
phrases.notes: Both of these items lead into the discussions that follow

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun on the previous עמוד
steps.mimraCoreRuling: These foods are not fed to the כהן גדול on ערב יום כיפור because they may cause קרי.

steps.title: The אורות in the פסוק are arugula
steps.stepSummary: Because arugula was just mentioned, the גמרא quotes a פסוק about gathering אורות. In the name of רבי מאיר, it is taught that אורות means גרגיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And one went out into the field to gather אורות' (מלכים ב ד:לט). It was taught in the name of רבי מאיר: this is arugula.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps aside from the כהן גדול. It explains a word in a פסוק, identifying the אורות as גרגיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a side-topic triggered only by the word גרגיר in the list. The new piece of information is a word definition: the plant called אורות in נביא is arugula.

keyTerms.meaning: A plant named in the פסוק; here identified as arugula
It was taught in the name of

phrases.english: "And one went out to the field
phrases.notes: מלכים ב ד:לט, the story of אלישע

phrases.english: to gather orot",
it was taught in the name of Rabbi Meir:
This is arugula.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַיֵּצֵא אֶחָד אֶל הַשָּׂדֶה לְלַקֵּט אוֹרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Side-topic triggered by the mention of גרגיר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The אורות of the פסוק are גרגיר.

steps.title: Why arugula is called אורות
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that the name comes from the fact that arugula 'lights up' (strengthens) the eyes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Why are they called אורות? Because they light up the eyes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains the reason behind the name אורות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אורות is connected to אור, meaning light. The name is taken to show that this plant is good for eyesight. This prepares the ground for רב הונא's practical advice in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: They light up (here: strengthen the eyes)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Why is their name called 'orot'?
Because they light up the eyes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the name given in step 2
steps.mimraCoreRuling: גרגיר is called אורות because it benefits the eyes.

steps.title: How to use arugula for the eyes
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא advises: if you find arugula, eat it if you can. If you cannot, pass it over your eyes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: One who finds arugula, if he can eat it, he eats it. If not, he passes it over his eyes.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives practical health advice that builds on רבי יוחנן's point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since arugula helps the eyes, eating it is best. If someone cannot eat it, rubbing it over the eyes still gives some of the benefit.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
One who finds arugula,
if he is able to eat it, he eats it,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לָאו — מַעֲבִירוֹ עַל גַּבֵּי עֵינָיו.
phrases.english: and if not, he passes it over his eyes.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמּוֹצֵיא גַּרְגִּיר אִם יָכוֹל לְאׇכְלוֹ אוֹכְלוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Practical use of the benefit described in step 3
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eat arugula if possible; otherwise pass it over the eyes.

steps.title: Which arugula is best
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא adds that this applies to arugula that grows on the border of the field.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: This is with border arugula.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא narrows רב הונא's advice to one kind of arugula. This closes the arugula side-topic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every arugula is equally effective. The kind that grows at the field's edge, unmixed with other plants, is the one that helps.

keyTerms.meaning: Of the border (from מֶצֶר, the edge of a field)

steps.whatToRemember: The arugula section is a side-topic: אורות means גרגיר; it helps the eyes; eat it or pass it over the eyes; the best kind grows on the edge of the field.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
With arugula of the border.
phrases.notes: Growing on the edge of the field

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The benefit applies to arugula that grows on the field's border.

steps.title: Advice for a guest: no eggs, no host's garment
steps.stepSummary: רב גידל quotes רב: a guest should not eat eggs and should not sleep in his host's garment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גידל said in the name of רב: A guest should not eat eggs, and should not sleep in the garment of the master of the house.
steps.whatsHappening: Going back to eggs from the list, the גמרא brings רב's advice for a guest about avoiding קרי while staying in someone else's home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eggs were listed as a food that may cause קרי. So a guest should avoid them. He should also not sleep in his host's garment, so that he does not dirty it and embarrass himself before his host.

keyTerms.meaning: A guest staying in someone's home

phrases.english: Rav Giddel said that Rav said:
A guest should not eat eggs,
and he should not sleep in the garment
of the homeowner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the item 'eggs' from the list in step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A guest should avoid eggs and should not sleep in the host's garment.

steps.title: רב and רב נחמן seek a wife while traveling
steps.stepSummary: On the theme of a person away from home, the גמרא reports that רב in דרשיש and רב נחמן in שכנציב would announce: who will marry me for the length of my stay?
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב came to דרשיש, he would announce: Who will be [my wife] for the days [I am here]? When רב נחמן came to שכנציב, he would announce: Who will be [my wife] for the days [I am here]?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells of a practice of two great אמוראים: when visiting a town, they would arrange a real marriage for the time they were there. This sets up the two challenges that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that a man away from home should not be without a wife. These were real marriages with קידושין, and they ended with a divorce when he left. The next steps ask how this practice fits with other sources.

keyTerms.meaning: Who will be [my wife] for the days [of my stay]?

steps.confusionAlert: מאן הויא ליומא refers to a full, halachically valid marriage with קידושין and a later גט. It is not something informal.

phrases.english: Rav, when he happened to come to Darshish,
would announce: Who will be [my wife] for the days [I am here]?
Rav Nachman, when he happened to come to Shechantziv,
would announce: Who will be [my wife] for the days [I am here]?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב כִּי מִקְּלַע לְדַרְשִׁישׁ מַכְרֵיז מַאן הָוְיָא לְיוֹמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of conduct away from home
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב and רב נחמן would marry a local woman for the length of their stay.

steps.title: Challenge: marrying in different places may lead to forbidden marriages
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the practice from רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. A man should not marry women in different places, because their children might later marry each other without knowing they are siblings.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: A man should not marry a woman in one country and then go and marry a woman in another country. Perhaps [their children] will be matched with each other, and a brother will end up marrying his sister (or a father his daughter), filling the whole world with ממזרות. About this it says: 'And the land will be filled with lewdness.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the practice of רב and רב נחמן using a ברייתא that warns against having wives in different places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a man has children in several towns, they may not know about each other. They could marry their own half-siblings and produce ממזרים. That is exactly what רב and רב נחמן seem to risk.

keyTerms.meaning: ממזר status; children born of forbidden unions

phrases.aramaic: וְהַתַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: But wasn't it taught: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יִשָּׂא אָדָם אִשָּׁה בִּמְדִינָה זוֹ,
phrases.english: A person should not marry a woman in this country,
and then go and marry a woman in another country,
lest they [the children] be matched with each other,
and it turns out that a brother marries his sister
(and a father marries his daughter),
and he fills the entire world with mamzerut,
and about this it is said: "And the land will be filled with lewdness."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַתַּנְיָא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the practice described in step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: The practice of רב and רב נחמן marrying in towns they visited
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Marrying in different places risks unknown half-siblings marrying each other, so how could these אמוראים do it?

steps.title: Answer: the children of רבנן are well known
steps.stepSummary: The answer: רבנן are famous, so everyone knows who their children are, and no mistaken marriage will happen.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: רבנן have a voice (are publicly known).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: the worry does not apply to famous Sages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's concern is only about children whose father is unknown to others. When the father is a well-known Sage, people know who his children are. So the risk of a hidden sibling marriage does not exist.

keyTerms.meaning: They have a 'voice'; they are publicly known

phrases.english: They say: The Sages have a 'voice' (they are publicly known).

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the ברייתא to people who are not well known
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The concern of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב applies to everyone, including רבנן
steps.terutzMaskana: Famous רבנן are excluded, since their children are publicly known

steps.title: Challenge: a woman who agrees to marry must count seven clean days
steps.stepSummary: A second challenge, from רבא: a woman who agrees to a proposal must wait שבעה נקיים before the marriage. So how could these Sages marry on the day they arrived?
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבא say: If they asked her to marry and she agreed, she must sit seven clean days?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem with the same practice: there seems to be no time for the required waiting period.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא rules that agreeing to marry may cause bleeding she does not notice, so she must count שבעה נקיים first. רב and רב נחמן announced the marriage only when they arrived. It seems the marriage could not begin right away.

keyTerms.meaning: They asked her to marry (a proposal)
Seven clean days counted before she may be with her husband

phrases.english: But didn't Rava say:
If they proposed to her to marry, and she agreed,
she must sit seven clean days?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, separate challenge to the practice in step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: The practice of marrying on arrival in a town
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A required seven-day wait after agreeing to marry makes a same-day marriage impossible

steps.title: Answer: messengers were sent ahead
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the Sages sent messengers ahead to announce their coming, so the woman could count her seven days before they arrived.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages would let them know ahead of time; they would send a messenger in advance.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second challenge. The announcement was made in advance by a messenger, not on the day of arrival.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a שליח went ahead, the woman agreed early and counted שבעה נקיים before the Sage came. So the practice fully fits רבא's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: They would act ahead of time

steps.whatToRemember: The practice of רב and רב נחמן survives two challenges. The worry about unknown siblings does not apply to famous רבנן, and the שבעה נקיים were counted because messengers were sent in advance.

phrases.english: The Sages would inform them [in advance],
they would act ahead of time
and send a messenger.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the facts of the case (the announcement was made in advance)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The announcement and the marriage took place on the same day
steps.terutzMaskana: Messengers announced it ahead of time, leaving time for שבעה נקיים

steps.title: Second answer: they only arranged seclusion, not a full marriage
steps.stepSummary: An alternative answer to רבא's challenge: the Sages only arranged a 'marriage' of seclusion and never planned to consummate it. So the woman did not need to count שבעה נקיים, and they still got peace of mind.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say instead: they only had the women set aside to be secluded with them. A person who has bread in his basket is not like a person who has no bread in his basket.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a different answer to the question from Step 10: how could the Sages marry on the very day they arrived? It says they never actually lived with these women as husband and wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 answered that messengers were sent ahead. This answer goes another way: there was no real marital relationship at all, so the woman had no need to count שבעה נקיים. The benefit was psychological. Knowing a wife is available calms a person's desire, just as a hungry man who knows bread is in his basket feels the hunger less.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you wish, say' (introduces an alternative answer)
They merely had them set aside or secluded with them (no consummation)
Bread in his basket: a picture of knowing that something is available to you

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers to רבא's challenge: (1) messengers were sent in advance, or (2) there was no consummation at all, only the comfort of having 'bread in the basket.'
steps.confusionAlert: This second answer does not add on to the messenger answer. It replaces it. Under this approach, no שבעה נקיים were needed at all.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say
they would merely have them set aside for seclusion (without consummating)
phrases.notes: Since no relationship took place, there was no need for שבעה נקיים.

phrases.english: because one cannot compare
one who has bread in his basket
to one who has no bread in his basket.
phrases.notes: Knowing a wife is available eases a person's desire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative to the answer in Step 11 for the challenge raised in Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the arrangement was seclusion and designation only, not a consummated marriage.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The Sages fully married these women, so the women would have needed שבעה נקיים first.
steps.terutzMaskana: No consummation took place, so no waiting period was needed. The purpose was only peace of mind.

steps.title: The כהן גדול is handed over to the priestly elders
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: the זקני בית דין pass the כהן גדול to the זקני כהונה. These elders take him up to בית אבטינס, make him swear, and then leave.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The elders of the court handed him over to the elders of the priesthood. They brought him up to the chamber of בית אבטינס, made him take an oath, took leave of him, and went on their way.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins, continuing the story of how the כהן גדול was prepared on the night before יום הכפורים. Here he moves from the court elders to the priestly elders.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the זקני בית דין had been reviewing the עבודה with him. Now the זקני כהונה take over and bring him to בית אבטינס, the chamber where the קטורת was prepared. There they give him an oath, which the next step spells out.

keyTerms.meaning: The elders of the court (the סנהדרין)
The chamber of the Avtinas family, who prepared the קטורת
And they made him take an oath

phrases.english: MISHNA: The elders of the court handed him over
to the elders of the priesthood
and they brought him up to the House of Avtinas,
and they made him take an oath,
and they took leave of him and went on their way.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ מְסָרוּהוּ זִקְנֵי בֵית דִּין לְזִקְנֵי כְהוּנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the גמרא's side-discussion and opens a new משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before יום הכפורים, the כהן גדול is passed to the זקני כהונה, who bring him to בית אבטינס and give him an oath.

steps.title: The wording of the oath, and the crying
steps.stepSummary: The elders tell the כהן גדול that he is their agent and the court's agent. They make him swear by God not to change anything they taught him. Then both he and they turn away and cry.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: 'My master, כהן גדול! We are agents of the court, and you are our agent and the agent of the court. We make you swear by the One Who made His Name dwell in this House that you will not change anything from all we told you.' He turned aside and cried, and they turned aside and cried.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives the exact words of the oath mentioned in the previous step. It also describes the emotional reaction of everyone involved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The oath reminds the כהן גדול that he serves as the court's שליח. So he must perform the עבודה exactly as the court taught, especially the קטורת, which he offers alone. The crying shows that the oath was painful: he was hurt at being suspected, and the elders were pained at having to suspect him.

keyTerms.meaning: The One Who made His Name dwell in this House (God)

steps.whyThisMatters: The oath protects the עבודה of יום הכפורים from being changed by a כהן גדול who might follow a different, non-rabbinic view. The גמרא will explain the reason for the oath and the crying.

phrases.english: And they said to him: My master, High Priest!
We are agents of the court,
and you are our agent and the agent of the court.
We make you swear
by the One Who made His Name dwell in this House
that you will not change anything
from all that we have told you.
He turns aside and cries,
and they turn aside and cry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the oath that the previous step only mentioned.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן גדול swears, as the court's agent, not to change anything in the עבודה.

steps.title: Keeping the כהן גדול busy with Torah through the night
steps.stepSummary: If the כהן גדול is a scholar, he teaches. If not, תלמידי חכמים teach in front of him. If he is used to reading ספרי תנ״ך, he reads. If not, others read to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he was a scholar, he would expound. If not, Torah scholars would expound before him. If he was used to reading, he would read. If not, they would read before him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה describes how the כהן גדול spent the night before יום הכפורים: with Torah learning, set up according to his own level.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The purpose was to keep him awake all night. The arrangement fits his ability: he leads if he can, and listens if he cannot. This applies both to דרשה (Torah explanation) and to קריאה (reading from תנ״ך).

keyTerms.meaning: Used to reading (from the written תנ״ך)

phrases.english: If he was a scholar, he would expound,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לָאו — תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים דּוֹרְשִׁים לְפָנָיו.
phrases.english: and if not, Torah scholars would expound before him.
And if he was used to reading, he would read,
and if not, they would read before him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the oath to how the night was spent.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן גדול is kept busy all night with Torah, either teaching or listening, depending on his ability.

steps.title: Which books did they read to him?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks which ספרים were read to the כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from what did they read before him?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks a short clarifying question. It is setting up the next line, which gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous step said 'they read before him' but did not say what. This question asks for that detail.

phrases.english: And from what do they read before him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the details of the reading mentioned in Step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which ספרים were read to the כהן גדול.

steps.title: Answer: איוב, עזרא, and דברי הימים
steps.stepSummary: They read from איוב, עזרא, and דברי הימים.
steps.simpleTranslation: From איוב, from עזרא, and from דברי הימים.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers its own question by listing the books that were read.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These books were chosen because they hold a listener's interest, which helps keep the כהן גדול awake.

phrases.english: From Job, and from Ezra, and from Chronicles.

steps.title: זכריה בן קבוטל: I often read him דניאל
steps.stepSummary: זכריה בן קבוטל reports from his own experience that he often read to the כהן גדול from דניאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: זכריה בן קבוטל says: Many times I read before him from דניאל.
steps.whatsHappening: A תנא adds a personal eyewitness report: דניאל was also read to the כהן גדול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds דניאל to the list of books. It is based on what זכריה בן קבוטל actually did in the בית המקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who served in the בית המקדש

steps.whatToRemember: On the night before יום הכפורים, the כהן גדול swears not to change the עבודה and is kept awake with Torah learning and with readings from איוב, עזרא, דברי הימים, and also דניאל.

phrases.english: Zekharya, son of Kevutal, says:
Many times I read before him from Daniel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further book to the list given in Step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דניאל was also read to the כהן גדול.
